::: {.ter-curriculum-hero}
::: {.ter-curriculum-kicker}
Ontario Technological Education · Reusable curriculum
:::

This open pathway helps students move from a real need to a communicated idea, a measured prototype, and an improved fabricated result. It connects the design process with digital design, laser cutting, 3D printing, manufacturing, and classroom projects without tying the learning to one course timetable.

<ol class="ter-design-cycle" aria-label="Design and fabrication learning cycle">
  <li>Design</li>
  <li>Communicate</li>
  <li>Fabricate</li>
  <li>Test</li>
  <li>Iterate</li>
</ol>
:::

## Learning pathway

<div class="ter-path-grid">
  <article class="ter-path-card">
    <p class="ter-path-number">01 · Start here</p>
    <h2>N.I.C.E. Design Process</h2>
    <p>Understand the situation, distinguish necessities from nice-to-haves, investigate existing solutions, generate alternatives, communicate a concept, prototype, evaluate, and begin the next iteration.</p>
    <p class="ter-path-action"><a href="01-nice-design-process/index.qmd">Learn the design process</a></p>
  </article>
  <article class="ter-path-card">
    <p class="ter-path-number">02 · Communicate</p>
    <h2>Digital Design &amp; Communication</h2>
    <p>Build visual literacy through raster and vector graphics, SVG, paths, exact geometry, logos, typography, layout, animation, user flows, and interface prototypes.</p>
    <p class="ter-path-action"><a href="02-digital-design/index.qmd">Build digital design skills</a></p>
  </article>
  <article class="ter-path-card">
    <p class="ter-path-number">03 · Fabricate in 2D</p>
    <h2>Laser Cutting &amp; 2D Fabrication</h2>
    <p>Progress from a first engraved plaque to calibrated fits, assemblies, measured tool holders, removable wall-and-bench modules, and an independent capstone.</p>
    <p class="ter-path-action"><a href="03-laser-cutting/index.qmd">Follow the laser-cutting curriculum</a></p>
  </article>
  <article class="ter-path-card">
    <p class="ter-path-number">04 · Fabricate in 3D</p>
    <h2>3D Printing &amp; Additive Manufacturing</h2>
    <p>Learn CAD, slicing, orientation, supports, tolerances, fasteners, functional parts, assemblies, repair parts, and evidence-based iteration.</p>
    <p class="ter-path-action"><a href="04-3d-printing/index.qmd">Explore additive manufacturing</a></p>
  </article>

    <p>A future pathway for CAM, work coordinates, toolpaths, workholding, end mills, pockets, profiles, and safe machine-specific practice.</p>
    <p class="ter-path-action"><a href="05-cnc-digital-machining/index.qmd">View the planned scope</a></p>

## TIJ1O Exploring Technologies and reusable Ontario technology resources

These lessons are used in TAS / Exploring Technologies and can support Ontario secondary school technology programs in different ways. Teachers can use the whole sequence or select a design process, communication, measurement, or fabrication lesson that fits a local project and available equipment.

::: {.ter-curriculum-relevance}
**Ontario curriculum relevance:** The complete pathway is especially useful for **TIJ1O Exploring Technologies**. Individual units transfer to **TDJ2O Technological Design**, **TMJ2O Manufacturing Technology**, **TGJ2O Communications Technology**, **TEJ2O Computer Technology**, **TCJ2O Construction Technology**, **THJ2O Green Industries**, and **TTJ2O Transportation Technology** where the learning genuinely involves design, measurement, prototyping, communication, or fabrication. Selected lessons can also support senior TDJ, TMJ, TGJ, TEJ, TCJ, and TTJ courses.
:::
